[0] Apple extends free usage period for its satellite features, allowing existing iPhone users an additional year. Apple disclosed this information in a footnote of the iPhone 18 Pro press release. Details are as follows.

[1] Apple confirms new round of extension arrangement

[2] Apple first introduced satellite connectivity in the iPhone 14 series, offering "Emergency SOS via satellite" and the ability to share location via satellite in "Find My." Apple stated at the time that the free usage period would be two years.

[3] Apple has since continued to expand its satellite features, including "Roadside Assistance via satellite" and "Messages via satellite." Apple now collectively refers to these as its satellite features.

[4] In November 2023, Apple extended the free usage period of "Emergency SOS via satellite" for existing iPhone 14 users by an additional year. Last year, Apple extended it once again, covering iPhone 14 and iPhone 15 users at the time, allowing them to enjoy all satellite features.

[5] Without further extensions, the free usage period for some users would have begun to expire later this year. However, Apple announced in a footnote of yesterday's iPhone 18 Pro press release that the free usage period would be extended by another year, now also covering existing iPhone 16 users.

[6] The press release content is as follows:

[7] Since Apple offers a one-year free usage period of satellite features for new iPhone buyers, users who purchase the brand-new iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo will automatically receive one year of free usage, while existing iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 16 users covered by the extension arrangement will also enjoy an additional year of free usage.

[8] Apple has yet to announce the收费标准 for satellite features after the free period ends. Since these features could potentially save lives, many speculate that Apple may ultimately decide to keep at least some features free, as charging users for emergency services could provoke controversy.

[9] Regardless, the free usage period has been extended by another year. Whether this is the final extension, or whether we will be writing similar reports again next year, remains unknown.

[10] Do you think Apple will eventually charge for satellite features? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
